source: NCERT Class IX, Contemporary India I, Geography Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Weather, Climate and the Monsoon
points: **Weather** = short-term atmospheric condition; **climate** = long-term average.
India has a **tropical monsoon** climate — the seasonal reversal of winds dominates.
**Monsoon** (from Arabic **'mausim'** = season) brings most of India's annual rainfall.

sections.heading: 2. Factors Controlling India's Climate
points: **Latitude** — the Tropic of Cancer divides India into tropical (south) and subtropical (north).
**Altitude** — the **Himalayas** block cold Central Asian winds, keeping India warmer.
**Pressure and winds** — the monsoon system, jet streams and the seasonal shift of pressure belts.
**Distance from the sea** — coastal areas have a **maritime (moderate)** climate; interiors **continental (extreme)**.
**Relief** — the Western Ghats cause heavy windward rain and a **rain shadow** to the lee.

sections.heading: 3. Mechanism of the Monsoon
points: Differential heating of **land and sea** creates low pressure over land in summer, drawing in moist sea winds.
The **Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)** shifts north in summer; the **jet streams** and the **El Niño/Southern Oscillation** influence the monsoon.
The **'burst' of the monsoon** (early June) brings sudden heavy rain; **Mawsynram/Cherrapunji** (Meghalaya) are the wettest places on Earth.

sections.heading: 4. The Four Seasons
points: **Cold weather (winter, Dec–Feb):** clear skies; NE trade winds; some rain in the NW (**western disturbances**) and SE (retreating monsoon).
**Hot weather (summer, Mar–May):** high temperatures; local storms — the **'loo'**, **Kaal Baisakhi** (Bengal), **mango showers** (Kerala/Karnataka).
**Advancing (SW) Monsoon (Jun–Sep):** main rainy season; Arabian Sea & Bay of Bengal branches.
**Retreating Monsoon (Oct–Nov):** monsoon withdraws; rain to the **Coromandel/Tamil Nadu** coast; **cyclones** in the Bay of Bengal.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: India = tropical monsoon climate; monsoon from Arabic 'mausim'.
Climate factors: latitude, altitude (Himalayas), pressure/winds, distance from sea, relief (rain shadow).
SW monsoon (Jun–Sep) = main rains; retreating monsoon (Oct–Nov) → Tamil Nadu.
Local winds/storms: loo (summer), Kaal Baisakhi (Bengal), mango showers (Kerala/Karnataka).
Wettest: Mawsynram/Cherrapunji (Meghalaya); ITCZ & jet streams influence the monsoon.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **SW monsoon (Jun–Sep)** gives most of India's rain; **Tamil Nadu** gets rain from the **retreating/NE monsoon**.
**Mango showers** are pre-monsoon showers in **Kerala/Karnataka**; **Kaal Baisakhi** in **Bengal**.
The **Himalayas** keep India warm by blocking cold northern winds.
The **rain-shadow (leeward) side** of the Western Ghats is dry.
